new_defect_types.name: slogan_injection
new_defect_types.description: Unrequested feel-good marketing copy (posters, banners, engraved rocks, tab labels) such as 'A BRIGHTER TOMORROW', 'For a Kinder World', 'CLEAN WORKSPACE SAFE SCIENCE' inserted into scenes. Text is spelled correctly, so A02/A03 never fire; it is a model-signature behaviour.
examples: orig53/gpt_image_2p5_sunburst_quality_high: rocks engraved 'A Happier Playlist Ahead', 'Pets Make Life Sound Better'
orig174/gpt_image_2p5_sunburst_quality_high: banners 'A BRIGHTER HUMAN TOMORROW', 'BEAUTY CONNECTS US'
phi176/gpt_image_2p5_sunburst: 'ROBOTS FOR A BRIGHTER TOMORROW'
phi50/gpt_image_2p5_sunburst_quality_high: 'CLEAN WORKSPACE SAFE SCIENCE'
new_defect_types.why_not_v2: B04 covers prompt words leaking into the image; B07 needs extras that change the scene. Correctly spelled, unrequested text that adds a message is not named anywhere. Suggest a B04 sub-clause: 'unrequested legible slogans/taglines' (minor; moderate when prominent).

new_defect_types.name: functional_graphic_state_mismatch
new_defect_types.description: A functional UI/graphic element contradicts itself: progress indicator not where the fill ends, two controls for one function, time shown three times, template field labels ('Title', 'Artist', 'Time') shown as content.
examples: orig53/qwen_image_2p1_pe: dark fill to mid-bar, caterpillar at the start; hedgehog 'Paused' plus a second pause button
orig53/gemini_3_1_flash_image: 'Title/Artist/Time' captions and times 03:45 / 04:20 / 04:20
orig53/krea2_turbo: slider thumb and caterpillar both mark progress
new_defect_types.why_not_v2: A18 checks alignment, overlaps and hierarchy, not semantics. A07 'duplicated UI card' partly fits. v3 A18 should add: 'state consistency — indicator, fill and labels agree; one control per function; no placeholder captions'.

new_defect_types.name: attribute_binding_to_wrong_entity
new_defect_types.description: A requested attribute appears on the image but on the wrong object (the colour of the elapsed path is painted on the caterpillar).
examples: orig53/fibo2_dev: caterpillar's rear segments dark green, branch stays brown
new_defect_types.why_not_v2: B05 asks whether the attribute is realised, so a judge sees 'dark green present' and passes it. Needs explicit 'bound to the right object' wording (the Layer B preamble mentions it but B05 does not).

new_defect_types.name: hose/cable_topology_error
new_defect_types.description: Linear flexible objects (hoses, cables, ropes) whose ends do not make sense: both ends run into the same reel, the held object is mid-span with a coupling, a hose dives into a puddle like a solid surface.
examples: phi294/flux3_klein: both hose ends go into the reel, gripper holds a mid-span coupling
phi294/krea2_turbo: gripper clamps the reel hub
phi294/qwen_image_2p1_nope: hose pierces a puddle with a splash
new_defect_types.why_not_v2: A10 is about manufactured objects working; A12 about cloth/liquid. Tracing a continuous object end-to-end is not prompted. Add to A10: 'trace hoses, cables, ropes, chains end to end'.

rubric_issues.problem: Left/right relative to a character facing the camera is ambiguous: 10 of 12 models placed 'to his left' on the viewer's left.
examples: orig414: crater viewer-left/prints viewer-right in fibo2_dev, flux3_klein, gpt_image_2, qwen models
rubric_issues.proposed_fix: State that 'his/her left' means the subject's own frame; when the subject faces the viewer this is the viewer's right. Either score a mirror swap as minor B06 or declare it tolerated, but define it.

rubric_issues.problem: Light direction vs. shadow direction is the most common photographic failure here, but A12 does not give a concrete check, and judges let 'shadow toward the light' and 'front-lit subject with a backlit shadow' pass.
examples: orig414/gemini: sun top-left, shadow goes left
orig414/flux3_klein: shadow toward camera, suit evenly front-lit
orig294/gpt_image_2p5_sunburst: one robe, two diverging shadows
rubric_issues.proposed_fix: Add explicit sub-checks: (1) shadows point away from the visible/implied light; (2) the lit side of the subject matches the shadow direction; (3) one occluder casts one connected shadow of matching shape; (4) a transparent object casts a light, caustic shadow, not a solid black one.

rubric_issues.problem: Requested text rendered tiny and illegible could be excused by the codec-limit rule.
examples: orig535/ideogram4_nf4: the warning line is a green scribble on a small screen
rubric_issues.proposed_fix: Rule 3 should state it never applies to text the prompt requests; illegible requested text is A02 (major if it is the requested headline) and B04.

rubric_issues.problem: Requested text repeated on a second unrequested surface (head screen + chest screen) and word-level duplication across a line break are not clearly assigned.
examples: orig535/qwen_image_2p1_nope: same warning on head and chest screens with different errors
orig535/qwen_image_2p1_pe: 'detected, system / system requires'
rubric_issues.proposed_fix: Clarify: repeated word inside the string = A02; the whole requested string duplicated on an extra surface = A07 (+B04 if the copies differ).

rubric_issues.problem: In UI mock-ups models paste photographic assets (photo hedgehog) into flat/cartoon UI. Album-art photos are legitimately photographic, so judges need a rule for which elements may be photographic.
examples: orig53/qwen_image_2p1_nope: photo hedgehog button next to clay caterpillar and flat icons
rubric_issues.proposed_fix: In UI/graphic mode, content panes (album art, thumbnails) may be any style; controls and icons should share one style. A photographic control in an illustrated UI is A15.

false_positive_traps.description: Prompt self-contradiction: 'slight camera shake suggests vibration' plus '1/1000s to freeze the spray'. A sharp image should not be penalised for missing shake under B05.
examples: phi533: all 12 images are sharp; none should get B05 for 'no camera shake'

false_positive_traps.description: Correct mirror reflections of text on a glossy car hood (reversed letters) are physics, not A03 pseudo-text.
examples: phi414/ideogram4_nf4: 'CITY SANITATION' reflected reversed on the hood

false_positive_traps.description: Cartoon hedgehog 'curled into a ball' with a face peeking out is a style convention; don't flag B03 unless the hedgehog is clearly uncurled (walking or lying in profile).
examples: orig53/gpt_image_2*: round spiky ball with face — fine
orig53/flux3_klein_base: walking hedgehog — flag

false_positive_traps.description: Rainbow caustics spread widely over a dark floor around a crystal sculpture under spotlights are plausible dispersion, not A23 over-processing, unless they appear where no light passes through the crystal.
examples: orig174/flux3_klein, gpt_image_2: strong rainbow patches

false_positive_traps.description: Licence plates, council names and street signs that are readable real-format text (e.g. 'BX70 KZV', 'Southwark Council') are not A03 defects; they may deserve C01 at most.
examples: phi414/gpt_image_2p5_sunburst_quality_high
phi414/gemini_3_1_flash_image

false_positive_traps.description: Robot push-ups on closed fists ('knuckle push-ups') match 'knuckle-like joints' and are not hand anatomy errors.
examples: phi176/gpt_image_2p5_sunburst, gpt_image_2p5_sunburst_quality_high
